top_changes.change: Replace the dashed white lane-line/chevron current markings with a flow-mapped water surface (foam ribbons, ripple normals, drifting debris and darker channel colour), and make restoration visibly calm the surface and shoreline instead of only dimming lines.

Build a hero Veilfall mountain matching the stronghold board: tiered cliff masses with green crowns, several broad falls and base spray, readable from First Shore; add natural shore ecology (rocks, driftwood, shrub pockets, varied sandbar shapes) to the flat dune islands.

Fix creature presentation polish: per-species hue-shift shinies instead of flat magenta overrides, distinct moving/hurt/rest poses, a grounded volumetric telegraph instead of thin magenta ellipses, and fight spacing that keeps the trainer out of creature bodies; also remove the floating saddle after dismount and the raw 'combat_char...' label keys in the fight HUD.

rows.reason: Islands now read as broad pale dune sand with sparse upright beach-grass clumps and damp darker shore edges, matching the dunes ruling; the grassy-dome/grey-skirt look is gone. Landforms are still smooth featureless sand humps with few rocks, driftwood or shrub pockets, so shore ecology layering remains thin.

Idle and moving cells for Cannonback, Ripplet, Riptusk and Mosshell are near-identical silhouettes; hurt frames differ only slightly (small head tilt), so the state is still unreadable without the label.
The Map tab shows a large black canvas with a single hex marker and 'Surveyed: 0%'; no terrain, coastline or route context is drawn.

Abyssal Guardian, Cragclaw, Mangrove Monitor, Riverdrake, Sirenseal and Torrentoad shinies are flat uniform hot magenta that erase all pattern and material; only some (Mosshell orange shell, Ripplet pink, Tidecoil teal, Aquaryn lavender) keep species identity.
No ground pickups are shown in these frames.

Up close (S3) Veilfall shows a broad white fall against dark faceted rock, but at distance (S2, creature sheets) it is still a narrow dark stone column with one thin white streak, nothing like the board's tiered, green-crowned multi-fall mountain.
The only named destination glimpsed is First Shore, which reads as a small cluster of a stone ring gate, crates and a tent on open sand; no distinct hall, arch or terrace landmark is legible.

The trainer now raises both arms in a stroke-like pose inside a foam ring, which no longer reads as relaxed wading, but the body is still fully vertical with legs/boots visible below the surface, so it reads as treading upright rather than a horizontal surface swim.
Riptusk, Aquaryn, Tidecoil and Torrentoad now lie collapsed on the sand, but Ripplet's faint still sits upright with its head raised and alert, and Torrentoad flips belly-up comically.

Menus are now a translucent blue-grey panel over the blurred world with teal tab underline and a creature portrait, giving some scenic connection; hierarchy is still weak, with uniform small grey text and identical boxed rows.
Build now has three illustrated cards and Players lists seats, but Quests and Players still leave the lower half empty around a few tiny text lines.

The few NPCs visible are small; the khaki hat-wearing guide recurs across swimming, mounted and camp frames with the same silhouette, and the First Shore NPCs share similar dark outfits. Named-role differentiation cannot be confirmed.

Water now grades from deep navy offshore to bright turquoise shallows with lighter rings around sandbars, giving real depth read; the gradient is still smooth and synthetic with little reef, rock or colour variation.

The telegraph is now a thin magenta outline ellipse instead of a filled slab, but it remains a flat bright magenta line slicing across both creatures and the HUD, and tells still depend on text banners ('incoming - move', 'HEAVY - get clear'); hit frames show almost no impact silhouette.
No catching frames are included.
The fight shown is against Cannonback; Riverdrake is not in the fight frames.

Exploration HUD is a set of compact corner panels (time, story objective, minimap, team, five-slot hotbar, health/food); it leaves the centre clear but still uses several dark boxed panels and the floating prompt text is small.
A white foam ring now surrounds the swimmer and no hard dark side-shadow is visible; there is still no trailing wake or splash to show forward motion.
No candy pickups are shown.
The team roster now sits on a dark backing panel with teal bars, so it no longer fades into terrain, though names and icons are tiny and hard to read.
No partly buried blue creature is visible behind Ripplet in any Venn fight frame.
The approach still shows a row of near-identical smooth tan oval sandbars with soft white-cyan halos lined up along the current, reading as placed stepping discs rather than natural shallows.

Quick bindings and controls are now a clean table with Gamepad and Keyboard columns (D-pad up, Left stick up), which scans better; text is still small grey on navy, and the map footer still lists literal key labels like [Minus] and [Comma]/[Period].
Live currents are drawn as evenly spaced white dashed lines with chevron arrows on a lighter flat band, literally reading as road lane markings painted on the sea.
Restored state only dims the dashed lane lines (they remain visible) and drops the lighter band; sandbars, water colour and geometry are unchanged.
No dialogue frames are included.
The map header reads TIDEWAKE and the Tidewake tab is the boxed/highlighted one, with Meadows shown as the inactive tab.
No catch result frames are included.
No dialogue frames are included.
Riptusk's resting pose lies on its side with legs out and is nearly indistinguishable from its fainted cell; Torrentoad has no resting frame in these sheets.
No flying frames are included.
The trainer repeatedly stands inside or directly against Ripplet's body and Ripplet presses into Cannonback's head, so limbs and heads overlap in many frames.
The boss title card now sits in the upper-right corner and does not overlap Cannonback's shell or head.
Named characters are not shown in grass, but at Salt Crown dense tall pale grass still reaches the trainer's knees and hides lower costume; at First Shore NPCs stand on open sand and read fully.
No dialogue frames are included.
No fight victory frames are included.
Riverdrake fight-win frames are not included.
Aquaryn stands tall and upright on the water in an identical pose across frames 08-10 with a hard dark shadow on the surface and no wake, splash or bob; the rider is a small dark figure on its back.

The camera no longer sits behind Aquaryn's back; the trainer is clearly framed walking ashore, but a grey U-shaped saddle/harness object floats in mid-air above the trainer in every land frame, a new visible artifact.
No catching frames are included.
No catch-aim HUD frames are included.

The bed now reads as a woven basket rim filled with straw-orange bedding, more nest-like, but it is still a flat low oval with no cushion volume, and at Salt Crown it becomes a thin brown strip; the First Shore bed view is also blocked by a large brown creature mesh in the foreground.
The workbench is still a small narrow wooden table with one tiny vise-like object, dwarfed by the tent; in First Shore and Brine Steps crafting views the trainer and an NPC stand in front of it.
No flying frames are included.
